findings.statement: Phase 3 is complete at claim granularity. Forty-six R1-R6 and controlling claim-source pairs were independently checked against current source and original or official sources. The audit assigns 20 SUPPORTED, 8 PARTIALLY_SUPPORTED, 1 CONTESTED, 9 UNSUPPORTED, 4 MISATTRIBUTED, and 4 INFERENCE_ONLY labels. Seed existence is not treated as remedy validity. D-071 remains a post-drop extrapolation with unquantified model uncertainty and no evaluated scientific predicate, not a completion prediction or a physics result. No hypothesis was constructed, ranked, or promoted.
assumptions_used: Current local source and registered audit documents establish repository facts; papers establish only claims within their stated equations and models.
Natural units, N=ln(a), q=ap, flat-FLRW no-QKE F-10 scope, finite electron mass, and Q positive into neutrinos are unchanged.
Absence claims are bounded to the sealed evidence set unless an exact current-source search is cited.
counterevidence_refs: No new trajectory, endpoint, code, test, benchmark, or gate execution occurred in this assignment.
A mechanism citation cannot establish current-operator applicability, full-prefix cost movement, or endpoint authority.
reproduction: Filter claim_audit by label and require every UNSUPPORTED, MISATTRIBUTED, and CONTESTED item to have phase4_action=REMOVE_PREMISE or REMOVE_CITATION.
Require every PARTIALLY_SUPPORTED item to retain its stated model and evidence boundary.
unresolved: Exact current channel nullspaces, projected non-null spectrum, reaction-tail and abundance enclosure, and a full-path temperature-clock certificate remain absent from the audited evidence.

findings.statement: R1 survives source audit only as two separated statements: the Rust spectral path has a stable logit conversion with strict-open raw failure, and the Python false-success taxonomy requires a software outcome contract. Neither statement proves that a coordinate change repairs all solver paths. PRIMAT baryon conservation is unrelated to R1 and is removed as a citation.
assumptions_used: Finite floating-point saturation to f=0 or f=1 is an admission failure, not a value to clip.
Failure/status precedence is software semantics, not a consequence of Fermi statistics.
counterevidence_refs: Open coordinates can still saturate numerically and do not define terminal-cause precedence.
PRIMAT arXiv:1801.08023v3:217-222 concerns baryon normalization, not occupation coordinates or solver admission.
reproduction: Inspect occupation_from_logit, occupation_values, and the underflow test; separately inspect the adjudicated false-success findings.
unresolved: No audited evidence maps every NumPy/Python outcome surface to the Rust physical-state admission path.

findings.statement: R2 has direct support for flat-FLRW finite-mass electromagnetic thermodynamics and energy-transfer temperature equations. PRIMAT supports plasma-temperature/scale-factor relations and numerical inversion in its stated FLRW models. It does not prove a sealed positive lower bound for alpha=-d ln(T_gamma)/dN, a globally single-valued inversion for the current collision-coupled path, or any nonzero-shear extension. SciPy event documentation supports only software event semantics, not cosmological transversality.
assumptions_used: Q>0 is energy transfer into neutrinos, giving the opposite electromagnetic debit.
A temperature coordinate is admissible only on a monotone branch with alpha bounded away from zero.
counterevidence_refs: The transfer term can alter the sign margin; the named evidence contains no full-path alpha lower bound.
The primary paper is FLRW and does not derive Type-I shear work.
reproduction: From the local equations compute dT_gamma/dN=[-3(rho_em+P_em)-Q/H]/(d rho_em/dT); only form dN/dx=1/alpha after certifying alpha>0 with margin.
unresolved: A sealed full-path alpha bound and EOS inversion certificate are missing.

findings.statement: R3 retains a mechanism-level derivative fact only. Froustey-Pitrou-Volpe derive O(N^4) finite-difference collision-Jacobian cost versus O(N^3) structured differentiation and report N/5 in their implementation. Current Rust has analytic occupation/network blocks and finite-difference temperature/density blocks. No cited source establishes a scale-admissible matrix-free Jv, an affinity/expm1 formulation, or exact per-channel discrete nullspaces for current bytes, and the paper's N/5 is not a RABBIT speed prediction. V2 directly conflicts with treating Jacobian work as a D-071 endpoint remedy.
assumptions_used: Electron-pair channels exchange energy with the electromagnetic bath; a universal neutrino-energy nullspace is invalid.
QKE and flavour-oscillation claims are excluded; only the classical collision-derivative algebra is compared.
counterevidence_refs: V2 reports a 77x-694x miss even with Jacobian construction deleted.
SciPy documents dense/sparse Jacobian interfaces, not a matrix-free Jv contract or physical nullspaces.
reproduction: Read arXiv:2008.01074v2 section 4.1 lines 285-304 and compare its stated implementation to the current Rust write_jacobian and thermal_bbn jacobian blocks.
unresolved: Current channel-specific detailed balance, left nullspaces, and scaled full Jv remain to be derived rather than assumed.

findings.statement: R4 is supported only at the requirement level. Grohs et al. directly demonstrate coupled multi-energy transport feedback into thermodynamics, scale-factor/temperature phasing, n/p, light-element histories and N_eff; PRIMAT explicitly says an energy-density treatment cannot fully capture weak-rate effects of spectral distortion. Current positive quadrature nodes/weights and FD moment tests do not imply a reaction-tail, weak-rate, or abundance enclosure. No audited source supplies the requested simultaneous rigorous enclosure.
assumptions_used: The certificate must cover the actual finite-mass reaction kernels and the outputs consumed by BBN.
A design requirement inferred from coupled sensitivity is not itself a proved error theorem.
counterevidence_refs: Neither paper derives a RABBIT-specific tail bound.
Positive quadrature and equilibrium moment convergence do not control nonlinear collision loss or weak kernels.
reproduction: Compare Grohs et al. abstract statements on coupled observables and PRIMAT section II.6's weak-rate limitation with the exact scope of the local moment tests.
unresolved: Reaction-tail, weak-kernel, Yp, D/H and N_eff propagated bounds are absent.

findings.statement: R5's AP source is valid only as a generic checklist for hyperbolic relaxation systems: constant conserved rows QR=0, a uniquely parameterized equilibrium manifold, consistent/well-prepared data, and stiff-accuracy caveats. It does not establish those properties for the current Fermi collision operator. V2 directly rejects the tested fixed momentum-cut slaving route, including its absent usable gap, three-dimensional genuinely gapped tail and at-most 1.25x model. V2 neither proves another invariant-aware AP route works nor universally rules one out. Applicability therefore cannot enter Phase 4 as a premise; only the need to derive Q and measure the projected spectrum may proceed.
assumptions_used: Generic AP theorems apply only after their operator hypotheses are verified for the actual discretization.
Logical non-exclusion is not positive evidence of existence or usefulness.
counterevidence_refs: The AP paper studies a different equation class and supplies no current RABBIT spectrum or channel invariant.
V2 finds no momentum-cut separation and says the stall mechanism remains unmeasured.
reproduction: Read arXiv:1009.2757 equations (14)-(15), the initial-layer discussion, and stiff-accuracy remark; then compare each precondition to the missing-evidence list.
unresolved: Exact current Q, a grid-stable projected non-null spectrum, overlap/handoff and response enclosure are absent.

findings.statement: R6 has supported bounded falsifier ingredients: local collisionless temperature/time signs, strict-open raw failure, combined first law, EOS limits, and exact stoichiometric baryon/charge checks; PRIMAT independently states baryon normalization; SciPy documents event crossing, counters and termination status. One line citation is corrected: collisionless df(q)/dN=0 follows from rhs occupation entries remaining zero at isotropic_boltzmann.rs:231-237, not from lines 192-209. Static limits and API documentation do not certify a trajectory, independence, or mutant-killing power; that stronger premise is removed.
assumptions_used: Each invariant is asserted only in its model and channel domain.
A proposed metamorphic test is not effective evidence until it kills a specified mutant or counterexample.
counterevidence_refs: Static physical-prefix/JVP receipts are not trajectories.
SciPy success/status semantics do not establish RABBIT raw physical admission.
reproduction: Inspect the cited local tests and functions; separately read SciPy event and return-value documentation.
unresolved: No executed mutant suite shows that the proposed R6 falsifiers catch the retained stall or false-success classes.

Keep physical coordinates and software outcome taxonomy as separate premises.

Retain the temperature clock only as a conditional object requiring a sealed transversality certificate.

Retain V2 as a fixed-cut negative result and require exact Q/spectrum/handoff derivation before applicability can be claimed.
R6: Correct the collisionless df(q)/dN citation to lines 231-237.
Remove any static-to-trajectory or unexecuted-mutant efficacy inference.
